programme.title: ¡Atención Obras!
programme.desc: Un programa ágil, variado y divulgativo; que incluye entrevistas, reportajes y además cuenta con una plantilla de destacados colaboradores especializados. Cada semana, el programa refleja la actualidad y aporta recomendaciones en el ámbito de la escena (teatro, danza, ópera), la música, las artes plásticas y el patrimonio cultural.

programme.title: Página 2
programme.desc: Magacín divulgativo sobre el mundo de los libros. Presentado y dirigido por Óscar López, el programa utiliza un tono ameno, entretenido y cercano en el que tanto el lector habitual como el ocasional encontrarán toda la información necesaria para satisfacer su interés por la lectura. Con una duración de treinta minutos y estructurado en diez secciones, "Página Dos" recoge los principales temas de la actualidad literaria y editorial en completos reportajes y presenta las novedades editoriales más interesantes. Cada semana cuenta con la presencia de escritores punteros que hablan sobre sus libros más recientes y de artistas que explican cuáles son sus hábitos de lectura. En la sección de cine, Desirée de Fez analiza un clásico de la literatura que haya sido llevado a la gran pantalla.

programme.title: 48 Hours
programme.sub-title: Closing the Cold Case of Robin Lawrence
programme.desc: A gifted artist is murdered in her home; decades later, her killer reveals what drove him.

programme.title: 48 Hours
programme.desc: The murders of a beloved doctor, his wife and their young daughter leave their Santa Barbara, Calif., community reeling; a manhunt leads to the arrest of a suspect who prosecutors say is a conman.

programme.title: 48 Hours
programme.desc: When a young mother goes missing, trained tracker and detective Dakota Black launches an investigation that locates the murdered woman.

programme.title: 48 Hours
programme.sub-title: The Setup Murder of Kristil Krug
programme.desc: A stalker sends menacing messages to a young mother before she is murdered.

programme.title: 48 Hours
programme.desc: Decades after 16-year-old Molly Bish vanished, her sister turns to TikTok for answers.

programme.title: 48 Hours
programme.desc: "Survivor" contestant Joe Hunter says his sister, whose death was officially ruled a suicide, was murdered.

programme.title: 48 Hours
programme.desc: A gravely ill young woman is rushed to the hospital where doctors discover her body is full of lead, leading everyone to wonder who caused it.

programme.title: 48 Hours
programme.desc: A woman dies after an alleged accidental shooting in her bedroom; eight years later, surveillance audio upends the case.

programme.title: 48 Hours
programme.sub-title: The Mother I Wish I Knew
programme.desc: The daughter of a woman murdered more than 30 years ago worries she will lose her father when a new investigation ties him to the case.

programme.title: 48 Hours
programme.sub-title: The Sneak Attack on Katlyn Lyon
programme.desc: When Katlyn Lyon Montgomery dies in October 2022, her mother turns to TikTok to share her grief and demand justice, building an online community to help hold Katlyn's killer accountable.

programme.title: 48 Hours
programme.desc: When a teenager shoots two of his friends, he claims the shooting was triggered by a reaction to a popular prescription acne medication that caused him to experience homicidal thoughts.

programme.title: 48 Hours
programme.desc: More than 50 years after a teenage girl is murdered in small-town Nebraska, the long-dormant case comes together to make an arrest.

programme.title: 48 Hours
programme.sub-title: Sade Robinson and the Secret Beach
programme.desc: When a college student in Milwaukee vanishes after a first date, investigators race to retrace her final movements.

programme.title: 48 Hours
programme.desc: When remains found in a swamp are identified, friends are stunned; Mindi Kassotis was supposed to have died in a hospital; five months later, police say she was murdered, and focus on her husband, Nick, to unravel how she died twice.

programme.title: Hit!
programme.desc: U.S. agent Nick Allen (Billy Dee Williams) has his own idea about how to fight a war on drugs: go to the source...and cut the big-time traffickers down. Embittered over the drug-related death of his teenage daughter, Nick sets out to do just that.

programme.title: The Bad News Bears
programme.desc: A major surprise as one of 1976's top-grossing films. THE BAD NEWS BEARS is a movie about children that is refreshing, utterly believable, and quite cleverly funny.

programme.title: Bad News Bears in Breaking Training
programme.desc: The story picks up the Bears career a year after their infamous second-place finish in the North Valley League. Faced with a chance to play the Houston Toros for a shot at the Japanese champs, they devise a way to get Texas to play at the famed Astrodome.

programme.title: Bad News Bears Go To Japan
programme.desc: Caught in a clash of cultures and ready to wreak more havoc on Japan than Godzilla, the Bad News Bears are back this time the Bears are spirited off to Tokyo by a slick and sleazy con artist who sees in the team a perfect peg for a get-rich-quick scheme.

programme.title: Grease
programme.desc: Grease is the one that you want! Go back to high school with Pink Lady Sandy (Olivia Newton-John), leader of the bad-boy T-Birds, Danny (John Travolta), and a rockin' and rollin' all-star cast.

programme.title: Rockers
programme.desc: Night Flight Presents: Starring Leroy 'Horsemouth' Wallace and Richard 'Dirty Harry' Hall; ROCKERS is a story of oppressed Jamaican musicians getting even with the 'mafia types' in the business

programme.title: Monty Python and the Holy Grail
programme.desc: Grossing the highest box-office of any British film in the US when released in 1975, this "cult classic" comedy from the Monty Python team loosely follows the legend of King Arthur, along with his squire and his Knights of the Round Table.

programme.title: The Monster Squad
programme.desc: Young kids form a club that is devoted to monsters, but soon get more than they bargained for when Dracula adjourns to Earth, with Frankenstein's Monster, the Wolfman, the Mummy, and the Gillman.

programme.title: Airplane!
programme.desc: Voted “one of the 10 funniest movies ever made” by the American Film Institute, “Airplane!” is a masterpiece of off-the-wall comedy.

programme.title: Airplane II: The Sequel
programme.desc: There’s a mad bomber on board, the first lunar shuttle is about to self-destruct, the engines are not working, and worst of all, the flight crew discovers they are completely out of coffee!

programme.title: Caddyshack
programme.desc: It's the snobs against the slobs! While caddy Danny tries to impress elitist Judge Smails, a crude construction tycoon tries to get accepted at the country club, and a groundskeeper stalks a gopher.

programme.title: Planes, Trains & Automobiles
programme.desc: Neal just wants to fly home to Chicago for Thanksgiving with his family. But all he gets is misery. Misery named Del Griffith, a loud-mouthed salesman who leads Neal on a wild goose chase.

programme.title: Who's Harry Crumb?
programme.desc: John Candy is bigger, better, and more bumbling than ever as a soft-headed private eye determined to crack a kidnapping case.

programme.title: From Dusk Till Dawn
programme.desc: In this thrilling cult classic, two dangerous outlaw brothers head out on a wild crime spree. After kidnapping a father and his two kids, the bad guys head to a seedy Mexican bar for safety, but come face to face with blood-sucking vampires.

programme.title: The Faculty
programme.desc: A group of small-town high school students discovers their teachers are under the control of mind-controlling alien parasites. From a smart script by Kevin Williamson (SCREAM), and directed by action-expert Robert Rodriguez (FROM DUSK TO DAWN).

programme.title: The Crow
programme.desc: Visually stunning and action-packed, this hit movie, based on the comic book series, follows the return from the grave of a young rock guitarist who, along with his fiancée, is brutally killed by a ruthless gang of criminals.

programme.title: The Truman Show
programme.desc: Truman doesn’t realize that his quaint hometown is a giant studio set run by a visionary producer/director/creator (Ed Harris), that folks living and working there are Hollywood actors, and that even his incessantly bubbly wife is a contract player.

programme.title: Ace Ventura: Pet Detective
programme.desc: Ace Ventura, Pet Detective, is on the case to find the Miami Dolphins' missing mascot and quarterback, Dan Marino. He goes eye-to-eye with sharks, stakes out the Miami Dolphins, and woos and wows the ladies. He always gets his man...or beast.

programme.title: Ace Ventura: When Nature Calls
programme.desc: Africa's the place where Ace is on the case, setting out to rescue an animal he loathes - a bat! If you're ready to laugh like a pack of hyenas, if you want more fun than an industrial-sized barrel of monkeys, you'll know what to do. Heed the call.

programme.title: The Big Lebowski
programme.desc: Jeff Bridges, John Goodman, Steve Buscemi and Julianne Moore star in this Coen brothers’ cult comedy about the Dude, his buddies, a case of mistaken identity, kidnapping and bowling.

programme.title: Fertile Floods - Croatia's Wetlands
programme.desc: Every year, in the middle of Croatia, it's the same story: after the annual snowmelt, a huge flood wave spills out of the Alps toward Zagreb and Belgrade. This leads to an increase in the River Sava's water levels of some ten metres. The contents of more than ten billion bathtubs floods an area the size of Lake Constance, often for months on end, yet still the Croatian and Serbian capital is spared a flood disaster. One of the reasons for this is the fact that the Sava is able to flow unhindered. The annual floods not only create a natural retention reservoir for flood control: alongside the Sava lies a natural paradise, unique in Central Europe. In the species-rich, alluvial flood forests of the last major meadow landscapes of the continent, enormous predatory fish like the catfish lie in wait for prey. The fertile floodplains of the Sava are an important resting place for more than 240 bird species, including Hoopoe, great crested Grebe, little Egret, common snipe and pied Avocet. Old, domestic livestock breeds like the Turopolje pig and Posavina horse spend almost the entire year in the floodplains. They appreciate the alluvial meadows, keep puddles and mudholes open whilst wallowing and, as living lawnmowers, they ensure that the moist meadows aren't transformed into dense oak forests. Thanks to this traditional pasture farming, more than 700 pairs of white stork alone breed in the Lonjsko Polje National Park. The Sava Floodplains allow us to glance into the past of our continent and at the same time, illustrate just how flood protection for major towns can be perfected.

programme.title: Portugal's Nature Parks
programme.desc: The Parque Nacional Peneda-Gerês is the only national park in Portugal. An area of almost 700 square kilometers, located in the extreme north of Portugal. Barren and rocky ridges in the plateaus, contrast with large forests and lush ground vegetation in deep valleys, crossed by lakes and rivers. The park is known for its oak forests, which are predominantly pedunculate and Pyrenean oaks. Among the typical animals of the park are the small Garrano ponies, a very old breed of horse and the only one in Europe that still lives in the wild.

programme.title: Portugal's Nature Parks
programme.desc: The highest mountain range in Portugal is the Serra da Estrela. The episode embarks on a voyage of discovery to adventurous rock formations and villages steeped in tradition. The nature park is the largest protected area on the Iberian peninsula. In the mountain range we accompany the young scientist Ana Matos, who wants to breathe new life into old traditions, and cheese maker Maria Natália Lopes. She watches over more than 350 sheeps.

programme.title: Portugal's Nature Parks
programme.sub-title: South West Portugal: Alentejano and Costa Vicentina
programme.desc: In the southwest of Portugal lies the little known Parque Natural do Sudoeste Alentejano e Costa Vicentina. It encompasses a narrow coastal strip that runs along the coast to the south of Portugal. Sparsely populated, this coastal region, which was placed under protection in 1988, is considered one of the last intact ecosystems in Europe. The steep cliffs, the almost constant wind and high waves have ensured that mass tourism has not gained a foothold here. There are still near-natural forests and a diverse bird life.

programme.title: Portugal's Nature Parks
programme.desc: Madeira - Portugal's autonomous island in the Atlantic Ocean, is closer to the African coast than to the mother country Portugal, from which it is separated by about 900 kilometers. The island's name comes from Portuguese sailors who claimed the uninhabited isle for themselves in 1419. Madeira means wood and that was available in abundance. Almost the entire surface was covered by dense forest. Since 1982, two-thirds of the landscape has been protected.

programme.title: Portugal's Nature Parks
programme.desc: The "Parque Natural da Ria Formosa" is one of the largest lagoon conservation areas in Europe. Bordered by five natural islands. A mosaic of sandbanks, brackish and freshwater lagoons and salt marshes. In 2010, the "Ria Formosa" was chosen as one of the seven natural wonders of Portugal. It is a unique ecosystem: in the winter months, more than 20,000 birds gather here. In addition, the nature park has one of the largest seahorse populations internationally. More than half of all fish species in the Atlantic are said to spawn in the lagoon.

programme.title: Baltic National Parks
programme.desc: Soomaa National Park is one of Europes wettest wilderness areas. Floods, forests and wetlands create a landscape where canoes replace roads during the fifth season.

programme.title: Baltic National Parks
programme.desc: Gauja National Park in Latvia features diverse wildlife, red sandstone cliffs and a winding river that flows through forests shaped by long human history.

programme.title: Baltic National Parks
programme.desc: Lahemaa National Park on Estonias Baltic coast features ancient forests, rivers and peninsulas where nature has remained largely untouched.

programme.title: Baltic National Parks
programme.desc: The Curonian Spit is a narrow peninsula of dunes and forests shaped by destruction and recovery through careful human intervention.

programme.title: Bavarian Forest - Deep, Dark and Enchanted
programme.desc: After an unusual mass reproduction of bark beetles in the nineties, thousands hectares of old spruce forest were destroyed. Soon after, a new, healthier forest started to grow – a new primeval forest. Within a few years, in place of the former monoculture, a diverse forest developed, rich in spruces, ashes, beech and fir trees. Naturally, this diversity has in turn attracted new animal and plant species. Even lynx and otters returned and made Bavaria their home again.

The annual floods not only create a natural retention reservoir for flood control: alongside the Sava lies a natural paradise, unique in Central Europe. In the species-rich, alluvial flood forests of the last major meadow landscapes of the continent, enormous predatory fish like the catfish lie in wait for prey. The fertile floodplains of the Sava are an important resting place for more than 240 bird species, including Hoopoe, great crested Grebe, little Egret, common snipe and pied Avocet. Old, domestic livestock breeds like the Turopolje pig and Posavina horse spend almost the entire year in the floodplains. They appreciate the alluvial meadows, keep puddles and mudholes open whilst wallowing and, as living lawnmowers, they ensure that the moist meadows aren't transformed into dense oak forests. Thanks to this traditional pasture farming, more than 700 pairs of white stork alone breed in the Lonjsko Polje National Park. The Sava Floodplains allow us to glance into the past of our continent and at the same time, illustrate just how flood protection for major towns can be perfected.

programme.title: Portugal's Nature Parks
programme.desc: The Parque Nacional Peneda-Gerês is the only national park in Portugal. An area of almost 700 square kilometers, located in the extreme north of Portugal. Barren and rocky ridges in the plateaus, contrast with large forests and lush ground vegetation in deep valleys, crossed by lakes and rivers. The park is known for its oak forests, which are predominantly pedunculate and Pyrenean oaks. Among the typical animals of the park are the small Garrano ponies, a very old breed of horse and the only one in Europe that still lives in the wild.

programme.title: Portugal's Nature Parks
programme.desc: The highest mountain range in Portugal is the Serra da Estrela. The episode embarks on a voyage of discovery to adventurous rock formations and villages steeped in tradition. The nature park is the largest protected area on the Iberian peninsula. In the mountain range we accompany the young scientist Ana Matos, who wants to breathe new life into old traditions, and cheese maker Maria Natália Lopes. She watches over more than 350 sheeps.

programme.title: Portugal's Nature Parks
programme.sub-title: South West Portugal: Alentejano and Costa Vicentina
programme.desc: In the southwest of Portugal lies the little known Parque Natural do Sudoeste Alentejano e Costa Vicentina. It encompasses a narrow coastal strip that runs along the coast to the south of Portugal. Sparsely populated, this coastal region, which was placed under protection in 1988, is considered one of the last intact ecosystems in Europe. The steep cliffs, the almost constant wind and high waves have ensured that mass tourism has not gained a foothold here. There are still near-natural forests and a diverse bird life.

programme.title: Portugal's Nature Parks
programme.sub-title: South West Portugal: Alentejano and Costa Vicentina
programme.desc: In the southwest of Portugal lies the little known Parque Natural do Sudoeste Alentejano e Costa Vicentina. It encompasses a narrow coastal strip that runs along the coast to the south of Portugal. Sparsely populated, this coastal region, which was placed under protection in 1988, is considered one of the last intact ecosystems in Europe. The steep cliffs, the almost constant wind and high waves have ensured that mass tourism has not gained a foothold here. There are still near-natural forests and a diverse bird life.

programme.title: Portugal's Nature Parks
programme.desc: Madeira - Portugal's autonomous island in the Atlantic Ocean, is closer to the African coast than to the mother country Portugal, from which it is separated by about 900 kilometers. The island's name comes from Portuguese sailors who claimed the uninhabited isle for themselves in 1419. Madeira means wood and that was available in abundance. Almost the entire surface was covered by dense forest. Since 1982, two-thirds of the landscape has been protected.

programme.title: Portugal's Nature Parks
programme.desc: The "Parque Natural da Ria Formosa" is one of the largest lagoon conservation areas in Europe. Bordered by five natural islands. A mosaic of sandbanks, brackish and freshwater lagoons and salt marshes. In 2010, the "Ria Formosa" was chosen as one of the seven natural wonders of Portugal. It is a unique ecosystem: in the winter months, more than 20,000 birds gather here. In addition, the nature park has one of the largest seahorse populations internationally. More than half of all fish species in the Atlantic are said to spawn in the lagoon.

programme.title: North America's National Parks
programme.desc: North America’s National Parks are world famous and their breathtaking landscapes fascinate millions of visitors. This spectacular series will show you what happens beyond the lookouts. Everglades National Park is an American national park that protects the southern twenty percent of the original Everglades in Florida. The park is the largest tropical wilderness in the United States, and the largest wilderness of any kind east of the Mississippi River. An average of one million people visit the park each year. Everglades is the third-largest national park in the contiguous United States after Death Valley and Yellowstone. UNESCO declared the Everglades & Dry Tortugas Biosphere Reserve in 1976, and listed the park as a World Heritage Site in 1979, while the Ramsar Convention included the park on its list of Wetlands of International Importance in 1987. Everglades is one of only three locations in the world to appear on all three lists.

programme.title: mareTV: Newfoundland - Canada's Eastern Point
programme.desc: In Newfoundland, at the easternmost tip of North America, the landscape is pristine, dramatic, and very sparsely populated. In summer, icebergs occasionally drift along the steep cliffs. When the "Titanic" collided with an iceberg and sank just 300 miles off the coast of Newfoundland in 1912, the last radio messages were picked up in a small wooden hut on the Avalon Peninsula. Today, most Newfoundlanders live on Avalon. There are particularly many seabirds here. In Witless Bay, the newborn puffins are ready for their first descent into the Atlantic. But some stray onto the coastal road, attracted by the lights of the hotels and restaurants. In doing so, they run the risk of being run over. A team of volunteers saves the lives of countless young birds: The Puffin & Petrel Patrol goes out at night dressed in high-visibility vests to collect the puffins. Biologist Sabrina Wilhelm then brings them back to Green Island, home to the largest puffin colony in North America. Here, the birds catch up on what they should have done long ago: the first dive of their lives.

programme.title: Magical Moors
programme.desc: Wide open heaths, windswept and barren in winter, are transformed into wonderful carpets of white, fluffy cotton grass in summer. Large bears and wolves roam alongside delicately fluttering butterflies, the bubbling calls of black grouse and the enchanting trills of the great snipe. Moors, bogs and wetlands can be found all over in Europe. Everyone has at least heard about this habitat but most know little about it. It is an ancient yet largely unknown set of landscapes that is full of enchanting surprises. On a warm spring day, poisonous adders emerge from hiding to perform their impressive mating dance. As dusk falls, snipe gather on traditional leks, leaping and singing to impress the opposite sex. And deep down in the boggy marshes, glittering emeralds of sticky dew lure insects into the deadly arms of meat-eating plants. Magical Moors captures the quiet beauty of a spectacular landscape, and its often elusive wildlife, in stunning detail.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: It is one of the wildest roads in Asia: the Trans Sulawesi Highway. The adventurous road leads through Indonesia's fourth-largest island and takes people to spectacular destinations. To beautiful beaches, turbulent cities, or unique primeval forests.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: Far out in the "Wild West" of Canada lies Bella Coola. If you want to get to the small town on the Pacific, you have no choice: there is only one road leading there, the Bella Coola Highway. It is constantly monitored and yet remains dangerous. Gravel roads, narrow hairpin bends and steep mountain slopes make the highway in British Columbia a particular challenge.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: In the extreme north-east of Norway known as the Finnmark region, winters are freezing cold and snowy. Due to the location on the Arctic Ocean, the roads are prone to snow drifts. Every metre is a challenge and a journey into risk. An adventure for all those who set off into the fascinating and unique landscape, through a seemingly endless desert of snow.

programme.title: The most spectacular change of seasons - Spring
programme.desc: This film explores Central Europe and presents the nature from a perspective you have never seen before. Fascinating landscape footage in high-quality HD technology, coupled with spectacular Cineflex aerial views, take us on a journey through the hitherto unknown blazes of colour of the Central European region and its inhabitants. We show you paradise on earth and demonstrate how climate and astronomy determine our life cycle. While seasons change, we visit several different European habitats that - in their diversity, are exemplary of a Central European region. Mountains, water, forests and meadows: we return to each of these habitats at different times of the year and show how the rhythm of life of each of our protagonists follows nature's clock. The four seasons determine all of the coming and passing away; a highly complex interplay in the universe of life. We explore the wondrous worlds of the mysterious cycle of nature together with extraordinary people. Breathtaking landscapes enable us to experience the change of seasons at first hand.

programme.title: The Sun - Inferno in the Sky
programme.desc: On July 23rd, 2012, a massive eruption on the sun hurls a colossal cloud of solar matter into space. It’s the most severe sunstorm in 150 years. Fortunately, the Earth is not in the direct path of this solar ejection. But it’s only a matter of time before a violent solar storm hits us. When these clouds of charged matter reach our planet, they can wreak havoc in electrical systems.

programme.title: Portugal's Nature Parks
programme.desc: Madeira - Portugal's autonomous island in the Atlantic Ocean, is closer to the African coast than to the mother country Portugal, from which it is separated by about 900 kilometers. The island's name comes from Portuguese sailors who claimed the uninhabited isle for themselves in 1419. Madeira means wood and that was available in abundance. Almost the entire surface was covered by dense forest. Since 1982, two-thirds of the landscape has been protected.

programme.title: Portugal's Nature Parks
programme.desc: The highest mountain range in Portugal is the Serra da Estrela. The episode embarks on a voyage of discovery to adventurous rock formations and villages steeped in tradition. The nature park is the largest protected area on the Iberian peninsula. In the mountain range we accompany the young scientist Ana Matos, who wants to breathe new life into old traditions, and cheese maker Maria Natália Lopes. She watches over more than 350 sheeps.

programme.title: Wild Alpine Rivers - Life in the Extreme
programme.desc: What would happen to the mountains without water? They would turn into deserts, devoid of life and vegetation. But there are very few mountains without water on our planet. They take care of this themselves, creating their life’s element and taking water directly from the sky by entrapping the clouds around them. This water then collects on the flanks of the mountains, where it turns from rivulets into rivers, that flow out into the oceans. Mountains and water are symbiotic, a cycle that keeps life on earth going. Mountain streams slowly move along meadows before, only moments later, turning into the spray of waterfalls or small mystic lakes. What kind of life can be found in and around this mysterious cosmos? We will investigate the world of the rare Danube salmon and be there to see the Danube bleak spawn. We will follow giant wels catfish into their hideouts, see great crested grebes on their underwater hunting. We go diving under the ice of frozen mountain streams and lakes, discovering life where none was thought possible.

programme.title: Europe's far North - Lofoten and the Arctic Ocean
programme.desc: Lofoten is the rugged archipelago in the Norwegian Arctic Ocean. Whoever arrives here is really at the end. Moskenes is the end of the line, and anyone who wants to go further needs a boat or a plane. The only way to get to the open sea is via the Maelstrom, which is quite dangerous. On the outermost headland, there are only a few ruins left. The last inhabitants are long gone, a supply was hardly possible. But fishermen are on the way, mainly to catch cod. And there is the coastal administration, which takes care of broken sea marks and lighthouses. A visit to one of the luxurious ships of the Hurtig Line is not to be missed. They shuttle off rough coasts on an eleven-day trip between the Russian border and southern Norway. A floating workplace for a wide variety of professions. The island of Andøya is not served by the Hurtiglinie. It lies too far out in the Atlantic. One of the most important observatories in Europe is located here. A young woman, Sandra Blindheim, is the boss. She is responsible for the large laser that delivers important information to scientists around the world. On clear winter nights, there is a wonderful panoramic view of the aurora borealis.

programme.title: Myths of the Congo - Apes and Aliens
programme.desc: The Congo, mighty and deep like no other river - yet still a retreat and a habitat for several of our world's strangest animals. Our closest relatives live deep inside the dense jungles: three of the four giant ape species have made the Congo basin their home. Rich in extraordinary footage, the second episode of "Myths of the Congo" also presents exciting insights into one of the most mysterious and dangerous regions on earth.

programme.title: Myths of the Congo - Deep and Dangerous
programme.desc: The river that swallows all rivers - this is what the natives call it. In reality, the Congo, when considering its water masses, is the second largest and the deepest river in the world. At its source in the north of Zambia, it starts out as a mere trickle, but on its journey westwards it grows and grows, becoming ever mightier and with it, the animals, too: the shoebill stork hides in the dense papyrus. Metre-long pythons hunt for their prey in trees and huge hippos fight for power and respect in the water. To survive in the Congo, animals have to adapt to extreme conditions. Here, evolution has spawned unique creatures: fish with lungs, wings and those that go hunting on land. The Congo River feeds the second largest rainforest on earth. Here is the home of the forest elephant. Time and again, they are summoned to this one, magic place: the Dzanga Bay. Countless other forest dwellers join them. What makes this place so special?

programme.title: mareTV: Sardinia - Magical Island in the Mediterranean
programme.desc: Sardinia is the second-largest island in the Mediterranean. The Sardin-ians themselves say it's a "continent for itself", a virtual world of its own, full of magic: A beach, gleaming in unreal pink shades, red corals protect against the evil eye and the inhabitants seem to remain forever young. On Sardinia, the owners of luxury yachts adopt sheep, fish have gold in their bellies and a giant mussel supplies the material for legendary sea silk. No one is surprised, that the Madonna goes on a sea cruise once a year.

programme.title: Bavarian Forest - Deep, Dark and Enchanted
programme.desc: After an unusual mass reproduction of bark beetles in the nineties, thousands hectares of old spruce forest were destroyed. Soon after, a new, healthier forest started to grow – a new primeval forest. Within a few years, in place of the former monoculture, a diverse forest developed, rich in spruces, ashes, beech and fir trees. Naturally, this diversity has in turn attracted new animal and plant species. Even lynx and otters returned and made Bavaria their home again.

programme.title: Deadly Roads
programme.desc: Some risks on these autoroutes have natural causes: Extreme weather, avalanches and landslides. In some areas, the locals even believe that evil spirits kill travelers. But many of the dangers are man-made: robbers or terrorists lie in wait for travelers, and tough labor pressures, social hardship and greedy mass-transit businesses also cause tragic driving accidents around the world. In the 20th century alone, 35 million people died on roads worldwide - plus 1.5 billion injured! With the two-part "Death Roads - On the Road at the Limit," phoenix offers a documentary road movie along the world's most dangerous car routes.

programme.title: Deadly Roads
programme.desc: Roads are much more than just gray strips of asphalt that allow us to travel and trade. For centuries they have been lifelines of mankind, full of stories and history - and in certain countries and areas they also hold great dangers, much human suffering and death. Documentary filmmaker Oliver G. Becker ventured onto dangerous roads in New Zealand, Scotland and Australia for phoenix.

programme.title: mareTV: Corsica - Fascinating Mountain World in the Mediterranean
programme.desc: Corsica looks like an alpine landscape in the Mediterranean, an island with dramatic rock formations, romantic bays and proud inhabitants who see themselves first and foremost as Corsicans and only then as French. The Greeks in ancient times called the island Kalliste: the beautiful. We explore this fascinating mountain world in the Mediterranean.

programme.title: Wild Faces of Switzerland - Winter in the Swiss Alps
programme.desc: In the heart of Europe lies Switzerland. It’s a surprisingly big little country: small in area, but big on natural beauty. And, like its many languages and cultures, its scenic diversity is something really special, too: from mighty Alps, dense forests and lush green valleys, to mysterious moors and roaring waterfalls. Mediterranean lakes and craggy rock landscapes are all close together in one small geographical location. Switzerland has many wild faces – some familiar and some hidden. It’s a country that’s astonishingly rich in variety, wilderness and scenic wonder. Each episode of the series seeks to do justice to this diversity.

programme.title: Chiemgau, A Changing Landscape
programme.desc: A few thousand years ago, there were bare moraine ridges and barren meltwater valleys here. A landscape born in the last ice age, characterized by the edge of the Alps, gentle hills, moors, and lakes. And by cultural richness, not only on the islands in Lake Chiemsee, with their famous monasteries and castles. Long before King Ludwig II, the first people settled in the Chiemgau region. Finds of hunting weapons from the Neanderthal era prove that the land was inhabited even during the ice age, probably because there was plenty of game to hunt. During the Bronze Age, one of the most important trade routes from the mountains to the Alpine foothills passed through here. Then came the Celts and the Romans.

programme.title: Chiemgau, A Changing Landscape
programme.desc: Three times in the past two decades, the Chiemsee area has experienced "once-in-a-century" floods. Climate, wildlife, and landscape have changed, and it seems this transformation is accelerating. Species living in the flood zones are developing sophisticated survival strategies. Knot ants, for instance, place their queen in the middle and form a raft with their bodies, even conquering new habitats. Flooding is less of a disaster for nature and impacts humans more significantly.

programme.title: Project Antarctica
programme.desc: Why don't you do something sensible? - Tim, Michael and Dennis have heard this sentence more than once since their school days when they professed their dream jobs: Artist, photographer, filmmaker. And they went on to say that some dreams had to remain dreams, that work didn't have to be fun, but above all that it had to pay enough and be safe. A few years later, the three are working on their joint feature film. They put all their eggs in one basket and are determined to invest two years of working time to achieve their goal. Unpaid. It's not just any goal: the three want to travel to Antarctica. They want to find out whether it is possible to reach even the most distant destinations if you only want to. With ten boxes full of equipment, they set off on the 14,000 km journey to Antarctica. And thus on the journey of a lifetime...

programme.title: Project Antarctica
programme.desc: Why don't you do something sensible? - Tim, Michael and Dennis have heard this sentence more than once since their school days when they professed their dream jobs: Artist, photographer, filmmaker. And they went on to say that some dreams had to remain dreams, that work didn't have to be fun, but above all that it had to pay enough and be safe. A few years later, the three are working on their joint feature film. They put all their eggs in one basket and are determined to invest two years of working time to achieve their goal. Unpaid. It's not just any goal: the three want to travel to Antarctica. They want to find out whether it is possible to reach even the most distant destinations if you only want to. With ten boxes full of equipment, they set off on the 14,000 km journey to Antarctica. And thus on the journey of a lifetime...

programme.title: North Macedonia: Between Traditional Dances and Mini Navy
programme.desc: Northern Macedonia emerged from being a once constituent republic of the former Yugoslavia. Anyone wishing to discover unknown worlds has every chance of finding them in this young Balkan country, full of imposing mountains, lakes of crystal-clear water, original villages and centuries-old customs. Nevertheless, Northern Macedonia, which borders Serbia in the north and Greece in the south, considered to be one of the poorest countries in Europe.

programme.title: The U.S. East Coast
programme.sub-title: The U.S. East Coast, The City and the Sea
programme.desc: The journey up the coast continues through Delaware to suburban New Jersey, and onwards into the heart of Manhattan. In Delaware, famous as a corporate tax haven, we visit a winery. In New York City we zip around with a bicycle courier and then head out to Long Island for oysters.

programme.title: The U.S. East Coast
programme.sub-title: The U.S. East Coast, Surf And Turf
programme.desc: New Hampshire has only 19 kilometers of coastline and short summers, all the more reason Shauna Fraser takes every opportunity to be by the sea. In the sheltered harbor of Rye, Shauna also targets inner attitude with yoga on a paddleboard.

programme.title: Model And The Bushmen, The
programme.desc: This is the story of an incredible adventure: a young woman from Norway moves into the wild and joins the last Bushmen hunters in Namibia. Every morning, the women set out to forage and the men sneak into the bush to hunt, carrying little else but homemade bows and arrows as they walk through the wilderness.

programme.title: Meteor Menace
programme.desc: On February 15th, 2013, out of the blue, a meteorite exploded in the earth’s atmosphere above the Russian region of Chelyabinsk. The event is a reminder of the ever-present 'Meteor Menace' and the need to understand more about these missiles from outer space.

programme.title: Children of the Sun
programme.desc: Butterflies surely are the most fancied species inside the insect world. Their beautiful colouring and their graceful flight appeal to everyone. There are close to 4000 types of Butterflies – today many of them are endangered due to the loss of their habitat.

programme.title: Children of the Sun
programme.sub-title: Children of the Sun - Wild Bees
programme.desc: Most people associate honey producing insects with the name “BEE“. Few realize that there are over 560 different species of bees - most of them live their lives “busy as a bee“ but some “abuse“ other insects and others are even known to be murderers. The film “Wild Bees” shows the incredible diversity and the stunning adaptations of our “BEES” to various habitats and diverse living conditions. Fascinating fights, sensational performances, imposing structures and colorful individuals – the world of “Wild Bees” offers all of this and more.

programme.title: Bavaria's Alpine Kingdom
programme.desc: There are sparkling palaces from ice and snow, like those found in a fairytale. The icy castles are the phenomenal work of Mother Nature but man had a hand in the magnificent stone castles of the region. The spectacular and histrionic mountains of the Bavarian Alps challenge wildlife and the people who live there and the rocky ramparts of this mountain kingdom are built of limestone and fossil rocks that tell of its origins beneath the sea. Millions of visitors from all over the world come to Bavaria every year to witness the mysticism of the landscape. Kings and Queens, tourist and locals, all are welcomed in the fantastic alpine kingdom. Early summer often comes with the threat of storms that bring floods that scour the land and threaten many creatures. But farmers risk these dangers to take their herds to the highest pastures, where they can graze on the sweetest flower-filled meadows. And later from the high-quality milk produced by their herds, the famers make highly prized cheese. Humankind lives among eagle owls, chamoix, wild cats, stoats and ravens up in these mountains.

programme.title: Alpine Lakes - Dark Depths and Icy Heights
programme.desc: This is a nature documentary, which leads us into the fascinating world of deep mountain lakes. We conquer ice palaces of unsuspected beauty. In the freezers, in which elves, fairies and mountain trolls once did their mischief, we move, using a special breathing technique and with special cameras in search of nocturnal hunters, whose eyes are equipped with residual light amplifying receptors.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: Tanzania is known for its national parks, vast landscapes and wild roads. They make traveling a real adventure. We travel in trucks, buses and off-road vehicles from the Indian Ocean via the Serengeti to Lake Victoria, accompany huge herds of wildebeest, observe lions and rhinos - and show the lives of the people who live on and along the roads.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: In the far north-east of Georgia, on the border with Russia, the Abano Pass leads to lofty heights. At almost 3000 metres it is the highest passable road in the Great Caucasus. It winds its way up dizzyingly steep slopes. On wild paths, it leads through a fascinating landscape.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: India's state of Rajasthan is known for its ancient palaces, vast landscapes - and wild transport routes. For thousands of years, dromedaries served as the most important means of transport. Today, India's roads are considered fast-paced, chaotic and unpredictable. On a journey through the desert state, we discover its rough roads.

programme.title: Stories of the Mediterranean Forest: Sierra Morena
programme.desc: The Mediterranean Basin is one of the planet’s most biologically rich and complex regions. The crossroads of Europe, Asia and Africa is considered to be one of Earth’s biodiversity hotspots. A vast number of both animal and plant species unique to the region live in its various habitats. The Mediterranean Basin is located in one of the planet’s temperate zones. The subtropical climate makes it colder and wet here in winter, hot and dry in summer and mild and rainy in autumn and spring.

programme.title: Wild Switzerland
programme.desc: Gentle, green meadows, rugged rock faces, mysterious lakes, dense forests, tall mountains, low-lying river deltas, quietly meandering mountain streams and smack dab in the middle, a unique fauna - THIS is Switzerland! We trace the elementary power of nature and present animals and plants in landscapes that have hardly ever been touched by mankind. Switzerland is an alpine country, but it is also Europe's surge tank. Rivers such as the Rhine and the Rhone have their sources here. Glaciers, crevasses, icy cold caves and the underwater dome of the Verzasca are the unusual settings we chose for this film. We meet with rare, selected animal species and present their behavioural patterns, such as the Swiss or Arven jay, the lynx and albino catfish. Cold, wind, snow and extreme locations demand adaptation that make us marvel.

programme.title: North America's National Parks
programme.desc: Yosemite National Park is a place of superlatives: with towering cliffs and giant sequoias, home to coyotes, black bears and the most elusive of all: the bobcat. Watch this documentary with ist spectacular shots, aerial views and time-lapse shots and learn some new facts about the biodiversity in one of North Americas most spectacular National Parks.

programme.title: North America's National Parks
programme.sub-title: America's National Parks - Great Smoky Mountains
programme.desc: Great Smoky Mountains National Park is an American national park in the southeastern United States, with parts in Tennessee and North Carolina. The park straddles the ridgeline of the Great Smoky Mountains, part of the Blue Ridge Mountains, which are a division of the larger Appalachian Mountain chain. The park contains some of the highest mountains in eastern North America, including Clingmans Dome, Mount Guyot, and Mount Le Conte. The border between the two states runs northeast to southwest through the center of the park. The Appalachian Trail passes through the center of the park on its route from Georgia to Maine. With 12.5 million visitors in 2019, the Great Smoky Mountains National Park is the most visited national park in the United States.

programme.title: Rewilding: Back to Nature
programme.desc: Worldwide, there are various projects and approaches to give nature more space again. The aim is to create larger wilderness areas that develop with hardly any influence of humans - by reintroducing so-called key animal species and creating a network of wilderness corridors across entire continents. Rewilding promises to be a cost-effective form of conservation in which we can boost biodiversity and protect the climate.

programme.title: Montenegro - From the Black Mountains to the Beach
programme.desc: The Balkan land of Montenegro owes its name to the Black Mountains. But there is so much more: steep cliffs, deep gorges, picturesque lakes, orthodox monasteries, Venetian architecture, sandy beaches and even fjords like those of Norway. There are three climate zones alone in the Adriatic. The inhabitants still try to find their way between the challenges of a post-socialist system, the much-vaunted Balkan remoteness and the opportunities of a still almost completely undiscovered tourist destination in Europe.

programme.title: Legendary Paddle Steamers
programme.sub-title: Following the Scottish West Coast with "Waverley"
programme.desc: Rugged coasts, untouched nature and the rough climate of the Atlantic characterize the landscape on the west coast of Scotland. In the sounds and lochs of the Scottish West, "Waverley", the last seaworthy passenger steamship in the world, appears once a year. The side-wheel steamer was built in 1947 to carry out short ferry passages on the Clyde River. Today, "Waverley" circumnavigates almost all of Great Britain. The impressive ship was sold to the "Paddle Steamer Preservation Society" in 1974 for the symbolic price of one English pound. Since then, she starts her season off the Western Isles in Scotland every year in May.

programme.title: Legendary Paddle Steamers
programme.sub-title: Across the lake Vierwaldstättersee with the “Unterwalden”
programme.desc: Lake Lucerne in the heart of Switzerland stretches from the foothills of the Alps to the first three-thousand-meter peaks of the high mountains. Home waters of the paddle steamer Unterwalden. For two and a half years she was not on the water. Now, after the biggest renovation in her history, the life of the 110-year-old paddle steamer is starting all over again. Her first voyages, with all the imponderables and challenges for the crew, take her into a diverse, wild landscape, right into the mystical heart of Switzerland. In their territory, scenic contrasts collide: barren high moorland and gently rolling alpine meadows, modern tourist resorts and quiet mountain villages, caves hidden deep in the earth and snow-covered two-thousand-meter peaks. The Unterwalden is part of the oldest and largest fleet of paddle steamers so high above the sea. Here on Lake Lucerne, according to national legend, the three original cantons swore eternal allegiance to each other over seven hundred years ago. A land around which countless myths entwine and whose lifeline since the opening of the Gotthard Pass in the thirteenth century was the shipping traffic on the lake.

programme.title: Fertile Floods - Croatia's Wetlands
programme.desc: Every year, in the middle of Croatia, it's the same story: after the annual snowmelt, a huge flood wave spills out of the Alps toward Zagreb and Belgrade. This leads to an increase in the River Sava's water levels of some ten metres. The contents of more than ten billion bathtubs floods an area the size of Lake Constance, often for months on end, yet still the Croatian and Serbian capital is spared a flood disaster. One of the reasons for this is the fact that the Sava is able to flow unhindered. The annual floods not only create a natural retention reservoir for flood control: alongside the Sava lies a natural paradise, unique in Central Europe. In the species-rich, alluvial flood forests of the last major meadow landscapes of the continent, enormous predatory fish like the catfish lie in wait for prey. The fertile floodplains of the Sava are an important resting place for more than 240 bird species, including Hoopoe, great crested Grebe, little Egret, common snipe and pied Avocet. Old, domestic livestock breeds like the Turopolje pig and Posavina horse spend almost the entire year in the floodplains. They appreciate the alluvial meadows, keep puddles and mudholes open whilst wallowing and, as living lawnmowers, they ensure that the moist meadows aren't transformed into dense oak forests. Thanks to this traditional pasture farming, more than 700 pairs of white stork alone breed in the Lonjsko Polje National Park. The Sava Floodplains allow us to glance into the past of our continent and at the same time, illustrate just how flood protection for major towns can be perfected.

programme.title: Moon, The: Our Gateway To The Universe
programme.desc: We are on the verge of a new age of exploration: besides the plans of NASA and other space agencies, over the next years also privately financed teams are going to send unmanned vehicles to the Moon. The goal is to find a cheap and efficient way to travel there on a regular basis, and in the long term to build a permanent human base.

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.sub-title: Arusha Irvine and Angus Ashworth, Day 5

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.sub-title: Philip Serrell and Stephanie Connell, Day 1
programme.desc: Philip Serrell and Stephanie Connell start a Road Trip from Cockermouth, though there are doubts they'll make it to the Kendal auction when their classic car breaks down.

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.sub-title: Philip Serrell and Stephanie Connell, Day 2
programme.desc: Stephanie Connell has a surprise in store for birthday boy Philip Serrell as they cross Caledonia on the second leg of their Trip. Expect gold panning and a novel buy in a book shop.

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.sub-title: Philip Serrell and Stephanie Connell, Day 3
programme.desc: Philip Serrell and Stephanie Connell are cruising Caledonia in pursuit of profit. Phil eats a square sausage while Steph becomes puppet master. Who'll triumph at the auction in Hamilton?

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.sub-title: Philip Serrell and Stephanie Connell, Day 4
programme.desc: Phil Serrell and Steph Connell return to Scotland. While all roads point to Dunfermline for auction, Phil sets sail and Steph buys a paddle.

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.sub-title: Philip Serrell and Stephanie Connell, Day 5
programme.desc: It's experts Stephanie Connell and Philip Serrell's final outing in their classic car and they're in the northeast of England looking for winning wares. The deciding auction is in Darlington.

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.sub-title: Raj Bisram and Irita Marriott, Day 1
programme.desc: Experts Raj Bisram and Irita Marriott hit the road again, this time in a Vanden Plas Princess. They are winding each other up, cracking bad jokes and looking for exquisite antiques in Wales. It's going to be a hair-raising adventure!

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.sub-title: Raj Bisram and Irita Marriott, Day 2
programme.desc: Raj Bisram and Irita Marriott crisscross the Welsh border looking for antique goodies, but finding things that don't require two strong assistants to carry them is not easy.

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.sub-title: Raj Bisram and Irita Marriott, Day 3
programme.desc: It's all gold and silver on Irita Marriott and Baj Bisram's third leg. But it's not all heavy metal - they find their groove in Birmingham's reggae heartland before a surprise auction result.

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.sub-title: Raj Bisram and Irita Marriott, Day 4
programme.desc: Raj Bisram and Irita Marriott embark on a five-county tour of The Fens. On the way, they discover secret doors, prehistoric artifacts and time travel.

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.sub-title: Raj Bisram and Irita Marriott, Day 5
programme.desc: Irita Marriott and Raj Bisram head to the seaside in Lincolnshire. It's the last chance to hit the shops before their final auction showdown.

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.sub-title: Izzie Balmer and Mark Hill, Day 1
programme.desc: Jewelry expert Izzie Balmer and mid-century fan Mark Hill head to Wales in a 1987 Lotus Éclat to start off their new trip in Pembrokeshire. Magic tricks and a folding cake stand go to auction.

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.sub-title: Izzie Balmer and Mark Hill, Day 2
programme.desc: New best friends Izzie Balmer and Mark Hill battle for bargain antiques in the towns and villages of Carmarthenshire, including special negligee jewelry, pitch pine furniture, a woven tapestry and glassware.

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.sub-title: Izzie Balmer and Mark Hill, Day 3
programme.desc: Izzie Balmer and Mark Hill raid the antiques shops of Stroud, Cirencester and beyond. Their finds include 1950s modernist pendant, a Victorian tea kettle, a Royal Worcester Cup and a 19th century food container.

programme.title: El día de los enamorados

programme.title: La Celestina

programme.title: Una pareja perfecta

programme.title: Marsella

programme.title: 20-N: Los últimos días de Franco
programme.desc: Crónica de la prolongada y artificial agonía a la que fue sometido Francisco Franco, dictador de España desde el fin de la Guerra Civil hasta su muerte el 20 de noviembre de 1975.

programme.title: Pajarico
programme.desc: Manu, que acaba de cumplir diez años, hace su primer viaje a Murcia. Rodeado de huertas, mar, naturaleza y una exuberante y cálida familia, descubrirá su primer amor y los primeros signos de su vida como adulto.

programme.title: El camino de los ingleses
programme.desc: En Málaga a finales de los 70, Miguelito Dávila es un joven de alma inquieta a quien le acaban de quitar un riñón. Durante ese verano, él y sus amigos experimentarán al extremo con el sexo, la amistad, la violencia y el amor.

programme.title: Los lobos de Washington
programme.desc: Dos amigos pretenden timar y vengarse de un antiguo colega, quien se vale de cualquier medio para escalar posiciones. Pero no es la única acción que se está tramando en esta jauría de lobos únicos en el mundo.

programme.title: Incautos
programme.desc: Ernesto, un conocido estafador, tiene un nuevo socio: Federico, un timador elegante, astuto y metódico. La sociedad parece perfecta hasta que irrumpe Pilar, la antigua amante y socia de uno de ellos.

programme.title: El puente de la paz
programme.desc: Los caciques de dos pueblos rivales separados por un río acuerdan construir un puente que los una y comenzar a limar las asperezas que otros años habían tenido.

programme.desc: Félix, un simpático vendedor de pisos, quiere ser director comercial de su empresa. Lo malo es que ese cargo se lo merece Lola, una vendedora joven, con la que Félix se lleva mal y que para colmo es la amante de Emilio, el jefe de ambos.

programme.title: Amantes
programme.desc: Un muchacho, tras hacer el servicio militar, se instala en casa de una mujer. A partir de ahí, se debate entre dos amores: el de su novia y el de su amante, la mujer que le da cobijo. Finalmente, adopta una solución trágica.

programme.title: Los agentes del quinto grupo
programme.desc: Un grupo de agentes secretos liderados por Duran, le sigue la pista a un tal Barrier, para localizar a una peligrosa banda de delincuentes que está planeando un gran golpe.

programme.title: El Coyote
programme.desc: Corre el año 1848 y California ha sido anexionada por Estados Unidos. El joven César de Echagüe es llamado por su padre para que regrese de Europa y se oponga a los desmanes de la autoridad sobre la población.

programme.title: La noche que mi madre mató a mi padre
programme.desc: Isabel acepta organizar en su casa una cena de negocios para Diego, un importante actor argentino que negocia su participación en la nueva película de su marido. Pero cuando Carlos muere inesperadamente, Ángel y Susana sospechan de Isabel.

programme.title: La vida de nadie
programme.desc: Emilio es un hombre exitoso, padre ideal y con una esposa perfecta. Pero ha vivido de engaños, y cuando una encantadora joven se cruza por su camino, su falso equilibrio comienza a desmoronarse sin remedio.

programme.title: ¿De qué se ríen las mujeres?
programme.desc: Tras la muerte de su esposo, Lucy y sus hermanas se toman unas merecidas vacaciones en un club de playa.

programme.title: La vida alegre
programme.desc: Ana empieza a trabajar como médica en un centro de enfermedades de transmisión sexual a pesar de la oposición de su marido Antonio, también médico. Allí, Ana entra en contacto con personajes marginales que acuden a su consulta.

programme.title: Nacida para ganar
programme.desc: La vida parece anclada en el tiempo para Encarna en Móstoles: el mismo trabajo desde la adolescencia, el mismo novio, y pocas perspectivas de que la cosa pueda cambiar.

programme.title: Cara de acelga
programme.desc: Antonio, un vagabundo ligero de equipaje y sin rumbo fijo, espera, en una carretera que alguien lo lleve a alguna parte. Así, es como acaba en un pueblo, donde se verá involucrado en un plan para robar una valiosa pintura en un convento.

programme.title: Barrio
programme.desc: Javi, Manu y Rai son tres adolescentes que viven en un barrio periférico de Madrid que ven cómo el verano pasa monótono y aburrido en el suburbio. La falta de dinero, las chicas y sus ilusiones serán los temas que centren la vida de estos.

programme.title: El otro barrio
programme.desc: Tras verse envuelto en una serie de accidentes mortales y mientras dura la investigación, Ramón, un chaval de 15 años, huérfano de padre, ingresa en un centro de acogida. Allí encuentra un compañero en el parlanchín y débil Aníbal.

programme.title: Oh, cielos
programme.desc: A Pablo Ventura, un publicista amoral, seductor y divorciado, lo mata de un balazo Aurelio, un compañero de trabajo. Pero a Pablo no le ha llegado todavía la hora de morir, antes tendrá que hacer una campaña publicitaria.

programme.title: La venganza de Don Mendo
programme.desc: La venganza de un hombre que es condenado a morir por estar enamorado de una mujer casada. Don Mendo promete proteger el honor de su amada Magdalena, ante la injusticia de no poder mantener su amor a la vista de todos.

programme.title: The Walking Dead
programme.desc: Serie que presenta la aclamada serie de historietas de Robert Kirkman con el mismo nombre donde un Sheriff se ve en un mundo lleno de Zombies.

programme.title: El show de Tom y Jerry
El show de los looney tunes
Tom y Jerry
programme.desc: Un gato domestico persigue a un ratón para su cena, pero el escurridizo y audaz roedor siempre se las ingenia para frustrar cada intento de atraparlo.

programme.title: Los Picapiedra
programme.desc: Pedro y Vilma Picapiedra y sus amigos Pablo y Betty Mármol son dos fabulosas familias que sobreviven a la era de la prehistoria en la ciudad de Piedradura.

programme.title: Tenet
programme.desc: Un hombre debe viajar a través de un mundo crepuscular de espionaje internacional en una misión que se desarrollará en algo más allá del tiempo real.

programme.title: Auction Hunters: Rodeo Ton
programme.desc: 1970s El Toro mechanical bull used to train bull riders; silver WWII era banjo; a collection of 1800s handcrafted hunting duck decoys.

programme.title: Auction Hunters: Risk & Reward
programme.desc: Ton & Allen arrive late to an auction. They uncover vintage bear traps and a bounty of street art. If the pieces belong to the artist, RISK, it could be their biggest score ever. If not, they'll be stuck with forged knockoffs.

programme.title: Auction Hunters: Allen's Ruff Day
programme.desc: Ton and Allen head to an auction in Ton's hometown and end up battling with a big-mouthed buyer. They discover a pair of tranquilizer dart guns and also end up fighting with a K9!

programme.title: Auction Hunters: The Smoking Ton
programme.desc: WW2 Stuart M3 tank barrel and heavy duty tank treads; rare, collectors' 1890 silver inlayed humidor; high-end industrial meat slicer in the ultimate restaurant unit.

programme.title: Auction Hunters: Space Cowboys
programme.desc: With the pawn shop history, Ton and Allen start the next chapter of their careers with a bang. They uncover an antique WWII firearm and a Russian cosmonaut space suit, which could be their biggest find to date...if it's real.

programme.title: Auction Hunters: Top Gun Ton
programme.desc: Scale RC Viper FanJet aircraft with a potent jet engine; 1920s Gundlach Korona large format field camera used for photography expeditions. Ton pilots a plane, but crashes and burns.

programme.title: Auction Hunters: Ton Voyage
programme.desc: When a ruthless storeowner seems hell-bent on stopping Ton & Allen from scoring new items in Santa Barbara they fight back. The guys uncover a rare antique air-gun and a vintage wooden boat built for speed, if it floats!

programme.title: Auction Hunters: High Flying Ton
programme.desc: A nerdy auction buyer tests Ton and Allen's patience at a big container auction in Ventura. The guys discover a basket and burners for a hot air balloon and a 19th century German single shot rifle!

programme.title: Auction Hunters: Knuckle Dust
programme.desc: 1870s French Jarre Dolne Knuckle Duster revolver-knife-brass knuckle combo, a rare original George Rodrigue "Blue Dog" screenprint and a 1980 autographed Raging Bull movie poster.

programme.title: Auction Hunters: Gangster Whiskey
programme.desc: Allen and Ton trek to an auction in Moreno Valley, CA, where two locker wins yield a vintage jukebox, a valuable baseball card and a Prohibition-era moonshine still.

programme.title: Auction Hunters: Whip It Good
programme.desc: With a motocross bike and a rare stock whip up for grabs, Ton and Allen face one of their toughest competitors yet: their former employee Carolyn, who knows all their tricks, has money to burn and is out for revenge.

programme.title: Auction Hunters: Ton's Got a Gun
programme.desc: In the affluent area of Mission Hills, CA, Allen and Ton pick up an estate unit that contains a minibike, a Depression-era slot machine and an 1871 Colt revolver.

programme.title: Auction Hunters: The Fall Guys
programme.desc: The pressures of running a shop are taking a toll on Ton and Allen and not even the discovery of a stunt-man's fall bag can ease the tension. When things get heated, Ton abandons the partnership and leaves town.

programme.title: Auction Hunters: You Foos You Lose
programme.desc: When their truck breaks down, Ton and Allen lay it all on the line to raise money to fix her. They score a Foosball table, Tommy Gun drums and to Ton's delight, a treasure trove of Twinkies, but will it be enough?

programme.title: Auction Hunters: Haff-Inated
programme.desc: Allen's off his game without his morning coffee, but some fun items help him re-energize. The guys find a wrestling ring, and when Allen uncovers vintage animatronics, they remind him of his days as a theme park boat captain.

programme.title: Auction Hunters: Battle Bought
programme.desc: Mint 1800s French "Harmonica Pistol" and a collection of '90s remote controlled combat robots.

programme.title: 112 en acción
programme.desc: Esta semana acompañamos a la Guardia Civil durante el dispositivo especial de seguridad de las Fiestas de Almendralejo. Los agentes realizan controles preventivos para evitar la entrada de armas, drogas y otros objetos que puedan poner en riesgo la seguridad durante las celebraciones. En uno de los puntos de control, un vehículo intenta esquivar el dispositivo por una pista cercana, pero los agentes consiguen interceptarlo y pronto descubren por qué trataba de evitar el control. La mañana se le complica a un repartidor cuando una rama de un árbol se incrusta en la caja de carga de su camión, destrozando por completo uno de sus laterales. La Policía Local de Cáceres acude para ayudar a liberar el vehículo sin que la estructura termine de ceder y levantar el atestado que permita determinar las responsabilidades. Los bomberos de Badajoz reciben el aviso de un incendio en una vivienda situada en una décima planta. Todo apunta a que el fuego se originó en un aparato de aire acondicionado exterior, prendió el toldo y terminó extendiéndose hacia el interior de la vivienda. Al tratarse de un incendio en altura, los bomberos tienen que adaptar la intervención para conseguir que el agua llegue con la presión necesaria hasta la planta afectada.

programme.desc: Concurso familiar donde se puede ganar un cuantioso bote con solo responder bien a cinco preguntas. Presentado por Alicia Senovilla. El objetivo es no caer eliminado y llegar a la fase final en la que tan solo dos participantes tendrán la oportunidad de subir hacia la cima del elemento más icónico del programa: la famosa escalera. Solo aquel que lo consiga tendrá opción de jugar por un gran bote que crece día tras día.

programme.title: RAZOR: Flower Power Mining
programme.desc: Every year, the world mines for billions of tonnes of metals. And the way we do it often comes at a huge cost to the environment. Nickel is one metal in huge demand as a vital component of electric vehicle batteries. One solution is blooming in an unexpected corner of the world in the form of a very special and unique plant called Odontarrhena decipiens. This is a type of hyperaccumulator, a plant which naturally takes up a large amount of certain metals, like nickel, from the soil. The plants are then processed to extract the nickel. The process, known as phytomining or agromining, is more efficient and less energy intensive, than traditional mining. RAZOR's Reya El-Salahi meets Professor Aida Bani, an instrumental part of Albanian phytomining research, who has dedicated two decades to studying this special type of plant. In Northern Albania a start-up is growing a stunning site of hyperaccumulator plants on a larger scale. Metalplant are cultivating 7 hectares with the aim of producing Nickel. They are also using enhanced rock weathering to make the process carbon negative.

programme.title: Integration and Empowerment - A New Paradigm of Sino-German Cooperation Driven by Technological Innovation
programme.desc: For the first time, the Sino-German Forum on Cooperation and Development of New Energy Vehicles and the VDA Round Table of Presidents/CEOs of German Suppliers in China will be jointly held as a combined event during the World New Energy Vehicle Congress (WNEVC). The forum brings together industry leaders to explore collaborative development in the NEV sector, covering topics such as industry trends, innovation, policy frameworks, and international cooperation.

programme.title: Architecture Intelligence: When a skyscraper goes deep
programme.desc: Beneath the bustling metropolises, there often exists an intricate underground network where access corridors and subway tracks intertwine. Have you ever wondered how it is possible to construct a skyscraper above metro lines without causing disruptions to the daily commute of thousands? Discover the answer in this clip from Tech It Out's documentary "Architecture Intelligence."

programme.title: Architecture Intelligence: Super bridge above the Yangtze
programme.desc: The mighty Yangzte poses a significant challenge for bridge builders. Let's witness how architects overcome this obstacle by constructing China's longest-spanning dual-purpose suspension bridge over this untamed river. Watch this clip of Tech It Out's documentary "Architecture Intelligence" for more.

programme.title: Meet China: From Little Toys to Global Factories, How Chinese Creativity Travels
programme.desc: In this episode of Meet China, we explore how “Made in China” is taking on new forms. A monster toy becomes a global collectible, an ocean park in southern China turns wonder into repeat visits, and a smart EV factory in Zhejiang shows how cars are built for overseas markets. In central China’s Xuchang, a small city supplies much of the world’s hair products, while in Guangxi, an Italian chef blends pizza with traditional medicinal food. From blind boxes to electric vehicles, wigs and a yam-and-lamb pizza, this episode reveals how Chinese creativity, scale and culture are reaching the world in unexpected ways.

programme.title: How China's ocean kingdom makes billions
programme.desc: In Southern China, a theme park you've likely never heard of is attracting more annual visitors than Hollywood Universal. The question is, how? Meet Chimelong Ocean Kingdom. It holds seven Guinness World Records and features the largest aquarium on earth. CGTN's Yu Hongyu dives into the strategy behind the splash to see how a local park created a hundred-billion-dollar opportunity.

programme.title: China's Kungfu theme park: A wild ride back in time
programme.desc: At Wansuishan Martial Arts City in central China’s Kaifeng, Henan Province, you’re not just a visitor - you’re part of the story. Every segment in the park is part of an immersive experience rooted in Chinese martial arts and traditional culture. From live matchmaking shows to iron flower performances, from Song Dynasty streets to interactive stages, this uniquely Chinese theme park – with not even one roller coaster or scary ride – was able to record over 24 million visits in 2025.

programme.title: Bizfocus: From myth to reality: How tech brings Eastern imagination to life
programme.desc: Ever wondered what China’s version of “Adam and Eve” or “Beauty and the Beast” looks like? While the world’s theme parks are all about Western fairy tales, one Chinese park took a different path—Fantawild brings ancient Eastern myths to life with mind-blowing tech and art. In this episode of Bizfocus, CGTN’s Xu Yi and her new friends from Pakistan and Bangladesh go for adventure in Fantawild Oriental Heritage in Mianyang, Sichuan. Gods, legends, and the tech behind the magic—all in one epic trip.

programme.title: BizTalk: China-US economic & trade watch
programme.desc: Global markets are closely watching the trajectory of China-US economic and trade ties. In this episode of BizTalk, CGTN's Michael Wang speaks with Jiang Wenran, founding director of the China Institute at the University of Alberta, and Lyu Xiang, research fellow at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences. They look ahead to how bilateral economic and trade ties could evolve over the next few years.

programme.title: The AI revolution is here - but are we ready for what comes next?
programme.desc: In this special joint episode of World Economic Forum and CGTN, hosts Robin Pomeroy from World Economic Forum and Guan Xin, CGTN Anchor, sit down with Professor Arun Sundararajan of New York University's Stern School of Business, a member of the WEF AI Governance Alliance and author of The Sharing Economy. They dive into the most pressing questions about artificial intelligence. From the future of employment to the deepening divide over AI governance and technological sovereignty, this conversation brings together perspectives from the US, China, and the global stage on how AI is reshaping economies, societies, and geopolitics.

programme.title: Highland industries, high-quality future
programme.desc: From smart ranching to vegetable greenhouses, from cold-chain logistics to cross-border trade… We take a look at Xizang's industrial transformation and see how the plateau is leaping into a new era of development.

programme.title: Discovering Guizhou: Miao culture extravaganza
programme.desc: What do spicy peppers, handmade guitars, and green cities have in common? Guizhou. In our new on-the-ground mini-series ChinaHorizons, we invite you to join our trip to Guizhou province. For the first stop, we record our podcast in a traditional Miao people's village cluster to appreciate diversified cultures, intangible cultural heritage items and delicious local cuisines.

programme.title: NAVIGATING GLOBAL ECONOMIC CHANGE | Exclusive with WEF President
programme.desc: The year 2026 marks the 20th anniversary of the establishment of the World Economic Forum's Beijing Representative Office. CGTN's Guan Xin speaks with Alois Zwinggi, president and CEO of WEF, to look back on nearly five decades of cooperation between WEF and China, examine the future of globalization and explore how 'China Opportunity 2.0' can further advance global cooperation in supply chain resilience, green technology and AI governance.

programme.title: Tennis Australia exec on the Australian Open's China push
programme.desc: China is taking center court in the Australian Open's global growth strategy. The Grand Slam has kicked off its 2027 China campaign in Beijing, aiming to engage fans through localized digital content, live events, retail and Chinese cultural Ambassadors. Tennis Australia says its long-term investment is paying off, with China now one of the tournament's largest international markets.

programme.title: China-US partnerships fueling rapid growth
programme.desc: Starbucks landed in China when coffee was a novelty. Today, 1 in 5 stores globally is there. American fast food and retail giants placed the same bet, and cashed in. Now local brands are out-executing them. The fix? Partner with Chinese private equity. Here's why it's working, and what it means for both sides.

programme.title: The green bridge between China & US
programme.desc: In 2019, Tesla was running on fumes. Shanghai handed it a lifeline, a gigafactory built in 10 months. Today, that plant produces nearly half of all Teslas using 95% local parts. That same playbook is expanding across green tech, pairing Chinese battery tech with American software. When the world's two largest economies build together, clean energy gets cheaper and faster for everyone.

programme.title: Reforesting Iceland
programme.desc: The stark and austere landscape of Iceland is iconic and one of the most noticeable traits is a lack of trees. The Icelandic ecosystem is classified as one of the most degraded in Europe, having experienced one of the worst cases of deforestation in the world. When viking settlers first arrived in Iceland, the land was covered in birch forest. But after hundreds of years of sheep-grazing, soil erosion and eruptions, Iceland was left with just 0.5% forest cover and a big problem: how do you grow trees in one of Europe’s largest deserts? RAZPR's Gabrielle Lawrence heads to the remote corners of south Iceland to meet Samson Harearson and Hrefna Jensdóttir from Iceland's Land and Forest Service working on an ambitious project, to grow trees in a treeless land.

programme.title: Farmed with China: Vietnam's food trade levels up
programme.desc: How is Vietnam's cassava industry reaching global markets? With technical support and cross-border cooperation with China, one crop is moving up the value chain — from local farms to international supply chains.

programme.title: Farmed with China: Thailand's farms go high-tech
programme.desc: As labor grows scarce, how can the land still yield abundant harvests? China-Thailand cooperation is providing solutions: machines for farmers, jobs in factories, and training for young agricultural engineers. Technology is more than equipment — it brings efficiency and hope.

programme.title: Cambodia's rice prawn=making more money!
programme.desc: Rice and prawn grow better together. Prawn loosens the soil and control pests, while rice cleans and oxygenates the water. One field, two harvests. A team from Shanghai Ocean University brought this eco-farming model to Cambodia, helping turn rice paddies into new sources of income.

programme.title: Laos farmers hack one season into many
programme.desc: Laos is transforming traditional agriculture into a modern locally-adapted system with the cooperation of China, applying benefits from a decade of seed innovation as well as the domestic development of potash resources. Alongside China-Laos Railway strengthening the supply chain, grain production is also gaining a stronger foundation. Explore the story in CGTN's special series Farmed With China.

programme.title: Working as one: Three Chinese villages pool resources for shared growth
programme.desc: Three villages in Shandong run on one shared economic ledger. It is a rural experiment in resource re‑allocation, pointing to alternative possibilities for rural communities across the developing world. In this episode of BizFocus, CGTN anchor Lincoln Humphries explores three villages in Dezhou, Shandong for their stories.

Discover more in CGTN's special series #FarmedwithChina. #Chinavsionary

programme.title: Farmed with China: Vietnam's food trade levels up
programme.desc: How is Vietnam's cassava industry reaching global markets? With technical support and cross-border cooperation with China, one crop is moving up the value chain — from local farms to international supply chains.

programme.title: Cambodia's rice prawn=making more money!

programme.title: Laos farmers hack one season into many
programme.desc: Laos is transforming traditional agriculture into a modern locally-adapted system with the cooperation of China, applying benefits from a decade of seed innovation as well as the domestic development of potash resources. programme.title: Working as one: Three Chinese villages pool resources for shared growth
